The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Regulation Crypto is here: State of Crypto. The SEC published its Reg Crypto proposal last week, giving the public 60 days to comment. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

XRP on track for biggest weekly gain in 21 months as Treasury buyback spurs 'curve control' hopes. XRP’s price has surged by 50% this week, the best performance since November 2024. Here's what's driving the rally. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto card spending tops $1 billion as stablecoins move into everyday purchases. Tracked card volume more than tripled in a year, with USDC and USDT funding over 70% of spending as users increasingly paid for groceries, rides and subscriptions. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto’s next billion users might be AI agents, and they’re paying with stablecoins. According to Coinbase’s head of AI product, we’re currently in the “Napster/LimeWire era” of agentic payments. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto exchange BitMart weighs partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after announcing shutdown. The exchange has hired White & Case as restructuring counsel, with a detailed roadmap expected by Sept. 9. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Web3 gaming network Sandbox stops Base and BNB chain bridging after exploit. The Sandbox disabled bridging on affected networks to isolate tokens and warned users not to trade SAND on Base and BNB, citing an impact of under 0.01% of supply. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,169 with a +0.43% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,443.28 with a +1.48% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

[...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. items.title: Geopolitical conflict and its impact on global markets - U.S. Bank
items.description: Geopolitics refer to events that influence the global landscape, including political or trade tensions and military conflicts. Such events often create economic uncertainty, which can lead to fluctuations in stock prices, interest rates, and currencies. Geopolitical conflicts frequently impact supply chains, such as Iran’s threats to halt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Wars in agricultural regions can also affect crop yields and deliveries. Events like these can cause supply-demand [...] History does not guarantee a quick recovery from every geopolitical shock, and markets can remain volatile when conflict disrupts essential supplies or broadens into the economy. Still, investors have often moved past the first wave of selling once they could assess the likely effects on growth, inflation and profits. A diversified portfolio and a clear investment plan can help investors participate when markets recover from the early negative impacts of major geopolitical events. [...] International markets face greater potential pressure because many European and Asian economies import a larger share of the energy they consume. The United States produces more of its own energy, but higher global prices still raise costs for American households and businesses. Recent market resilience does not eliminate geopolitical risk; it shows that investors continue to weigh conflict against the economy’s ability to absorb disruption.
